title: Newman's theorem for communication complexity
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite types, let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, and let $\varepsilon, \varepsilon', c \in \bbr$ satisfy $1 < c$ and $c\varepsilon < \varepsilon'$. Then the private-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error tolerance $\varepsilon'$ does not exceed the public-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error tolerance $\varepsilon$ increased by $\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)\rceil$, where $t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)$ is the derandomization sample count; that is,
\[
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{priv}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)
  \;\le\;
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}(f)
  \;+\;
  \bigl\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c) \bigr\rceil ,
\]
with both complexities taken as values in $\bbn \cup \{\infty\}$.
hypotheses_covered: X and Y are finite types
replaced:
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ with $X, Y$ finite, let $\varepsilon, \varepsilon' \in \mathbb{R}$
and $c > 1$ satisfy $c \cdot \varepsilon < \varepsilon'$.
Then the private-coin communication complexity of $f$ at error $\varepsilon'$ is at most the
public-coin complexity at error $\varepsilon$ plus
$\lceil \log_2(\mathtt{derandomizationSamples}\;X\;Y\;\varepsilon\;c) \rceil$:
\[
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{priv}}_{\varepsilon'}(f)
  \;\le\;
  \mathrm{CC}^{\mathrm{pub}}_{\varepsilon}(f)
  + \left\lceil \log_2\!\left(\mathtt{derandomizationSamples}\;X\;Y\;\varepsilon\;c\right) \right\rceil.
\]
In particular, switching from public-coin to private-coin randomness costs only
$O(\log(|X| \cdot |Y|) / \varepsilon^2)$ additional bits.
